correctness.rationale: The proof partitions X uniquely by its least entry valuation k. For 2k≥n, X²=0 automatically and the primitive Smith form diag(1,d) over the quotient of length e=n−k gives rank/image length 2e−v(d), counted by GL₂ and rank-one residue determinant fibers. For 2k<n, nonzero square-zero reduction is rank-one nilpotent with a cyclic vector; Cayley–Hamilton plus cyclicity make B²=0 mod π^(n−2k) equivalent to trace and determinant both zero mod that ideal. On a rank-one nilpotent residue chart the trace–determinant map has two independent unit partials and uniform q² lifts per digit; allowed traces have q^k values, and allowed determinant valuation classes contribute exactly the displayed q exponents. Counting every shell yields the polynomial and its total, with no division by two, including ramified/mixed characteristic. Image length r≤n follows from im⊂ker; vanishing homology iff r=n, giving the coefficient. Independently enumerated every 2×2 matrix modulo 2,4,8,16; 3,9,27; and 5,25, computing the defining four square equations and determinant valuation, and matched every coefficient, e.g. Z/16: (1,9,78,168,384). Small enumerations verify only listed rings; the uniform all-chain-ring statement uses algebraic chart proof.
residual_risks: Only finite commutative chain rings and 2×2 maps; does not classify similarity, higher-dimensional nilpotent matrices, nor schemes.
